finding.claim: The download handler joins the attacker-supplied query parameter f onto root with filepath.Join and reads the result with no containment check, so ../ sequences escape /srv/files and expose arbitrary readable files.
finding.source: Query parameter f, read at files.go:12 via r.URL.Query().Get("f"). Route /dl is registered at files.go:32 with no authentication, so any remote client can send it.
finding.sink: os.ReadFile at files.go:13 on filepath.Join(root, name); the bytes are written to the response at files.go:18.

trace.note: f is taken verbatim from the query string
filepath.Join calls Clean, so /srv/files/../../etc/passwd resolves to /etc/passwd, and ReadFile reads it
file contents are written to the client

finding.guards_checked: No rejection of .. segments; no Clean-then-prefix check against root; no filepath.Rel containment test; no os.Root or allow-list; no authentication or authorization on the route. Absolute paths are not a bypass because Join concatenates them under root, but .. traversal is sufficient.

verdict.guard_found: none. files.go:12-13 takes f verbatim and passes filepath.Join(root, name) straight to os.ReadFile; there is no ".." rejection, no Clean-then-prefix or filepath.Rel check, and no auth on the route registered at files.go:32. The only check, the err branch at files.go:14-17, is a NotFound response and does not limit what is read. The avatar handler's filepath.Base at files.go:22 is not applied to download.
verdict.reason: At files.go:12-13, f is joined onto /srv/files without containment, so f=../../etc/passwd makes filepath.Join clean to /etc/passwd and ReadFile returns it, which files.go:18 writes to the unauthenticated client on the /dl route (files.go:32).

finding.claim: Neither /dl nor /avatar checks identity or ownership, and the server listens on all interfaces over plain HTTP, so every file under /srv/files is served to any unauthenticated network client if those files are meant to be private.
finding.source: Any unauthenticated network client reaching port 8082.
finding.sink: Serving file contents from /srv/files via download (files.go:18) and avatar (files.go:28).

trace.note: ListenAndServe binds to :8082 on all interfaces, plain HTTP, error ignored

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, authorization, ownership check, TLS, or middleware in files.go. No README or config in the repository states whether the files are meant to be public, so intent is unconfirmed.

verdict.guard_found: none. files.go has no auth, ownership, TLS, or middleware. /dl (files.go:32) and /avatar (files.go:33) are registered bare, and ListenAndServe(":8082", nil) at files.go:34 binds all interfaces over plain HTTP with its error ignored. download reads and returns the file unchecked (files.go:13, 18), and avatar only takes filepath.Base (files.go:22).
verdict.reason: Anonymous network clients reach /dl and /avatar with no control between them and the os.ReadFile/w.Write sinks at files.go:13-18 and 23-28, so any file under /srv/files is readable if it is meant to be private; the candidate's trace lines are accurate. The candidate understates the impact: download joins the unsanitized query parameter `f` onto root (files.go:13) with no containment check, so `f=../../etc/passwd` escapes /srv/files because filepath.Join cleans the path after joining.
